prerequisites: Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus
Knowledge of functions with multiple variables

learning_outcomes.text: Students know common network structures and learning methods. They possess theoretical background knowledge and can assess the potential of neural networks. They know typical applications of neural networks and have learned to create and use neural networks for practice-oriented examples.

Students additionally possess basic knowledge in data analysis, statistics, and other methods of knowledge-based systems. The module partly repeats and deepens previously acquired basic knowledge from Mathematics 1 and 2 modules as well as Programming 1 and 2.

Students learn fundamental approaches to data analysis. They get to know the potential fields of neural networks and can use them to solve data-based problems. They learn to use some tools and libraries for creating and operating neural networks.

syllabus_topics: Theory of neural networks (Perceptron, Multilayer Perceptron, learning procedures, quality criteria, Deep Learning, generalization)
Application-specific neural networks (e.g., regression, image classification, time series forecasting)
Introduction to software libraries for creating and using neural networks
assessment_rules: The graded assessment can be a term paper (10-15 pages), a written exam (duration as per valid study regulations), or an oral exam (as per general examination regulations).
